newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA POLICE EFFORTS FOILED BY JUDGES-MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA POLICE EFFORTS FOILED BY JUDGES-MINISTER.

text.p: Romania's interior minister accused judges and prosecutors on Friday of jeopardising the government's anti-corruption campaign through carelessness.
"The result of police work is jeopardised by judges and prosecutors who allow offenders to walk free on medical grounds, even before the trial starts," Gavril Dejeu told a news conference.

Dejeu said judges and prosecutors were to blame for what he called careless handling of serious crimes and corruption cases in the Balkan country. Officials at the General Prosecutor's office were unavailable for comment.
Corruption and organised crime have spread quickly in Romania after the December 1989 overthrow of communist rule.
Timid attempts by the country's first post-communist authorities to fight crime made little headway.
Romania's new centrist government, which ousted leftists in elections last November, launched a tough campaign to fight corruption and crime.

Scores of corrupt policemen and magistrates lost their jobs and several prominent bankers and businessmen accused of fraud and mismanagement of funds were put behind bars as a result of the campaign led by President Emil Constantinescu.
But Dejeu said the compaign had failed to yield more results, despite increased efficiency in police work.
Police had investigated 23 percent more cases in the first half of 1997 than the same period last year, including serious cases of blackmail, robbery and fraud, Dejeu said.
But most of the culprits were at large after courts ruled they were too ill to stay in prison. Many of the rulings were based on forged medical certificates, he said. REUTER
